title: [PM-40851] Render the shared folder grid on the desktop vault view
body:
## 🎟️ Tracking

[Jira](https://bitwarden.atlassian.net/browse/PM-40851)

## 📔 Objective

Render the shared folder grid above the collection/item list in the desktop vault-v3 host.
This PR also updates the card grid component to only show 3 rows max based on the container width, per design.

## 🤖 Bitwarden Claude Code Review

**Overall Assessment:** APPROVE

Checked the new desktop `:vaultId/:collectionId` route against `apps/web/src/app/vault/individual-vault/vault-routing.module.ts` — it mirrors it guard-for-guard, and `vaultScopeGuard` already turns away a folder the user's collections do not hold or that belongs to another organization, falling back to the organization vault rather than the unscoped one. Traced the `vaultScope$` rewrite that now reads both segments through `resolveVaultScope`: `params.get("collectionId")` is `null` on the single-segment route and `parseVaultScope` short-circuits on that, `cipherInScope` narrows the item list to the drilled folder, and `collectionInScope` deliberately keeps the whole organization's collections — which is what `scopedCollections` must carry for the grid to build its tree and find the parent node.

Verified the width-responsive cutoff in the card grid: `floor((width + 12) / 252)` clamped to `[1, 3]` matches what `auto-fill` resolves `minmax(min(100%, max(240px, (100% - 1.5rem) / 3)), 1fr)` to at 240/300/492/600/744/1200px, and `auto-fill` (not `auto-fit`) keeps the track count independent of the card count, so `columns` is not measuring its own output. The `ResizeObserver` is disconnected on `DestroyRef` and re-attached when the list comes and goes, the signal-write-from-observer pattern matches `libs/components/src/layout/layout.component.ts`, and `libs/ui/common/src/setup-jest.ts` stubs `ResizeObserver` globally so the spec's local stub restores to a real value in `afterEach`. Every i18n key the component uses is present in `apps/desktop/src/locales/en/messages.json`, and the `tw-border-0 tw-border-t` pairing on `bit-accordion` is the same idiom used in `tab-header`, `filter-menu`, and the v2 table components.

The typechecking and browser build failures flagged on the previous review pass have cleared — `Run typechecking`, `Run tests - Desktop`, `Run tests - Browser`, and `Run tests - CLI` are all green on the current head.
